request.spec:
A steward can merge a person into another (a select of the other person and a merge button on
the row; PERSON_MERGED from=<name> into=<name>; anyone else, the same person, or either of them
retired, is refused with an error on the row). The merged person's claims move to the other
(numbers and dates kept, listed after the other's claims in the order they were added, each losing
any figure a statement bound); the merged name and aliases become aliases of the other; the merged
person's patrons are added to the other's (not themselves, no repeats), anyone naming the merged
person as patron names the other instead (no repeats), and the merged person's pool memberships move
to the other (shares added when the other is already a member). Their statements, holds, watchers
and contact are dropped. The merged person leaves the list (no row), and every total follows.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A steward can merge a person into another (a select of the other person and a merge button on
the row; PERSON_MERGED from=<name> into=<name>; anyone else, the same person, or either of them
retired, is refused with an error on the row). The merged person's claims move to the other
(numbers and dates kept, listed after the other's claims in the order they were added, each losing
any figure a statement bound); the merged name and aliases become aliases of the other; the merged
person's patrons are added to the other's (not themselves, no repeats), anyone naming the merged
person as patron names the other instead (no repeats), and the merged person's pool memberships move
to the other (shares added when the other is already a member). Their statements, holds, watchers
and contact are dropped. The merged person leaves the list (no row), and every total follows.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
A steward can now merge one person into another, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests. Before my change, only the merge test failed.

**How it works**
- **Endpoint:** `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{personId}/merge` with body `{ into, by }`. It is wired in `people/{personId}/merge.POST.yml` using the same step pattern as retiring a person.
- **Refusals:** `MergePerson` refuses anyone who isn't a steward, a merge into the same person, and a merge where either person is retired. Each refusal shows `person-error` on the row and writes nothing. It also refuses if either person was saved by someone else in the meantime, using the existing version numbers.
- **What moves:** `PersonRepository.merge` runs inside the request's transaction:
  - **Claims** move to the other person with their numbers, dates and settled figures kept, and lose any figure a statement bound. They are listed after the other's claims, in the order they were added.
  - **Name and aliases:** the merged name and its aliases become aliases of the other.
  - **Patrons:** the merged person's patrons are added to the other's, and anyone naming the merged person names the other instead. The other is never their own patron, and nothing is repeated.
  - **Pools:** memberships move to the other, and shares are added together where the other is already a member.
  - **Dropped:** statements, holds, watchers, grades and contact go, and the person row is deleted. No database migration was needed.
- **Audit:** `PERSON_MERGED from=<name> into=<name>` is written, followed by the usual ROLLUP and TOTALS lines when figures change.
- **Screen:** the new `features/merge/merge.slot.tsx` adds the `person-merge-into` select and the `person-merge` button to each row. After a merge it re-reads the whole sheet.

**Choices I made that the request didn't cover:**
- **Closed period totals:** a closed period stores a fixed total for each person. I add the merged person's figure to the other's, so the period's figures still add up. If you'd rather drop those figures instead, it's a one-line change.
- **Who the select offers:** it lists every other person, retired ones included. Choosing a retired person shows the error; they are not hidden from the list.
